items.name: White pepper
combinations: in pale soups and white gravies (invisible heat)
with honey for throat (maricha logic)
ground fresh over eggs and khichdi
items.preparation: Ripe peppercorns retted free of skin — maricha's heat without its dark husk notes. Slightly mellower than black; the same deepana engine underneath.

items.name: Mild paprika
combinations: colour for tandoori marinades without fire
in butter-gravy dishes (deghi role)
bloomed briefly in warm oil for full colour
contraindications: pitta excess in quantity (mild but still capsicum)
items.preparation: Ground mild red capsicum — colour first, warmth second. The kitchen's way to look fiery while staying kind to pitta-sensitive eaters.

items.name: Black turmeric
items.prabhava: The camphor-scented dark turmeric — a ritual and medicine rhizome more than a kitchen one; tribal traditions reserve it for pain, wounds and worship.
combinations: paste applied externally for sprains (folk use)
minute doses in tribal cough remedies
ritual use at Diwali and tantric worship
contraindications: internal use beyond minute traditional doses (potent essential-oil fraction)
items.preparation: Bluish-black rhizome, camphoraceous and intense — treat as a medicinal, not a cooking turmeric. Culinary use is rare and sparing; external and ritual use dominate.

items.name: Galangal root
combinations: bruised into tom kha and Southeast Asian soups
with lemongrass and makrut lime leaf (the classic trio)
thin slices in clear warming broths
items.reviewNote: Culinary (Thai/lesser) galangal entry; the medicinal greater galangal is authored separately as dravya.greater-galangal in batch-23 — reviewer may wish to cross-link rather than merge.
items.preparation: Pine-sharp rhizome sliced or bruised into simmering broths — harder and more resinous than ginger, it flavours rather than melts. Fish it out before serving.

items.name: Lemongrass
items.prabhava: The tea-grass — bhustrina brewed with chai or alone settles the stomach and cools feverish heat; Maharashtra's gavati chaha is folk medicine in a cup.
combinations: steeped with tea (gavati chaha)
with ginger for monsoon colds
bruised stalk in Southeast Asian curries and broths
contraindications: pregnancy in strong medicinal doses (essential-oil caution)
items.preparation: Fresh or dried blades and bruised stalks steeped or simmered. Citral does the work — digestive, calming, gently febrifuge; the rare aromatic that leans cooling.

items.name: Makrut lime leaf
combinations: torn into Thai curries and tom yum
with galangal and lemongrass (the aromatic trio)
sliced hair-fine over salads (Southeast Asian style)
items.preparation: Double-lobed citrus leaves torn or julienned into simmering dishes — the citrus perfume without the acid. Remove whole leaves before serving.

items.name: Dried fenugreek leaf
items.prabhava: The finishing bitter — a palmful crushed over a gravy in the last minute perfumes the whole dish; methi's medicine wearing restaurant clothes.
combinations: crushed between palms over butter chicken and dal makhani
in kadhi and paneer gravies
kneaded into thepla-family doughs
items.preparation: Sun-dried leaves of the Kasur methi strain, rubbed to powder over finished dishes off the heat. A little bitterness at the end civilises rich gravies.

items.name: Dried rose petals
items.prabhava: Hridya — pleasing to the heart in the classical double sense: shatapatri cools pitta, lifts mood and perfumes food, the gentlest of the medicinal flowers.
combinations: over kheer, phirni and sherbets
in thandai and summer milks
rose tea with fennel for pitta afternoons
gulkand when preserved in sugar (see rose petal preserve)
contraindications: none significant — among the safest of dravyas
items.preparation: Fragrant deep-pink petals dried in shade to keep colour and oil; crumbled over sweets or steeped as tea. Choose culinary-grade, unsprayed roses.

items.name: Vetiver root
items.prabhava: Khus in the kitchen — the green sherbet, falooda and matka-water flavour; culinary ushira carries the same daha-quelling coolness as the medicinal root.
combinations: khus sherbet over ice (the summer green)
in falooda and milk coolers
root bundle in the clay water pot
contraindications: synthetic 'khus essence' with artificial colour (choose real extract)
items.reviewNote: Culinary/spice entry for khus flavouring; the medicinal water-infusion root is authored as dravya.khus-root in batch-23 — reviewer may cross-link the pair.
items.preparation: True khus extract or syrup made from the fragrant root, used in summer drinks and desserts. The vivid green of bazaar sherbets is dye; the scent is the medicine.

items.name: Edible camphor
items.prabhava: Karpura — pungent yet cold, the paradox spice: a rice-grain crumb transforms a whole pot of payasam or paan; classical texts count it cooling, fragrant, kapha-pitta-hara.
combinations: a crumb in South Indian payasam and temple prasadam
in paan (tambula) blends
in chandana-karpura cooling pastes (external)
contraindications: synthetic camphor — never edible, toxic (only bhimseni/edible grade)
items.preparation: Only natural edible (bhimseni) camphor, in rice-grain pinches dissolved into sweets. The margin between perfume and poison is the pinch — respect it absolutely.

items.name: Betel leaf
items.prabhava: The classical after-meal rite — tambula-sevana: a fresh leaf after food sweetens the mouth, moves digestion and, the texts add, pleases the mind. The leaf alone is the medicine; its infamous companions are not.
combinations: plain leaf with fennel and cardamom after meals (the clean tambula)
with gulkand as meetha paan (no areca, no tobacco)
leaf juice with honey for children's coughs (folk)
contraindications: with areca nut or tobacco — the carcinogenic combinations, excluded from any recommendation
with slaked lime in quantity (oral mucosa)
items.reviewNote: Leaf-only entry. Areca nut (batch-18, betel nut) carries an engine-exclusion warning; the leaf without areca/tobacco/excess lime is the classical tambula and is treated on its own merits.
items.preparation: Fresh heart-shaped leaf, rib removed, taken plain or with fennel-cardamom-gulkand after meals. Everything wrong with 'paan' arrives with the additives, not the leaf.

items.name: Sesame chutney spice blend
combinations: over idli and dosa with a spoon of ghee or sesame oil
mixed into hot rice (podi sadam)
with jaggery in winter versions
contraindications: kapha weight-management in oily podi-sadam quantities
items.preparation: Roasted sesame ground with dried chilies, urad dal, curry leaves and salt. Tila's winter-warming, vata-settling oil in condiment form — a spoon, with fat, on hot grain.

items.name: Cubeb pepper
items.prabhava: Kankola — the tailed pepper of the paan tray and the urinary formularies: a mouth-freshening maricha cousin whose smoke-sweet heat classical and Unani texts aim at the bladder and chest.
combinations: chewed singly as mouth freshener (paan-tray tradition)
in Mughlai and Maghrebi spice blends
with elaichi for breath and voice
items.preparation: Tailed berries crushed fresh — allspice-adjacent warmth with a camphor lift. One or two berries chewed is the traditional freshening dose.

items.name: Stone flower
items.prabhava: The lichen that anchors goda masala and Chettinad blends — nearly flavourless raw, it blooms smoky-earthy in hot oil; the mystery depth in biryanis that guests cannot name.
combinations: bloomed in hot oil for biryani and Chettinad masalas
essential to goda masala (see goda masala)
in bisi bele bath powder
contraindications: source cleanly — lichens absorb their environment
items.preparation: Papery dark lichen fronds fried briefly in oil at the start of cooking. Contributes base notes, not top notes — the bass line of southern masala music.

items.name: Cobra saffron
items.prabhava: Raktastambhana — the classical styptic stamen: nagakesara steadies bleeding from piles and excess flow, and lends chaturjata its fourth, driest voice.
combinations: fourth member of chaturjata (see chaturjata blend)
with butter and sugar for bleeding piles (classical yoga)
pinch in rich Mughlai masalas
items.preparation: Dried golden stamens of the ironwood tree, powdered into blends or classical formulations. Culinary pinches season; gram doses medicate — keep the two apart.

items.name: Kapok bud
combinations: fried whole for bisi bele bath (its defining dish)
in Chettinad and Kannadiga masala pastes
with stone flower and dried coconut (the southern trio)
items.preparation: Dried caper-like buds of the silk-cotton (shalmali) tree, always fried in oil to open their flavour before grinding. A regional signature — one or two buds per pot.

items.name: Indian Sichuan pepper
items.prabhava: The numbing pepper — tumburu's electric tingle (sanshool compounds) anaesthetises the tongue as it warms the gut; Nepali chutneys and Konkani fish curries treat it as both spice and tooth-medicine.
combinations: in Nepali tomato chutney (golbheda ko achar)
teppal in Konkani fish curries
chewed for toothache (folk anaesthetic use)
contraindications: mouth ulcers (the tingle irritates broken mucosa)
items.preparation: Husks (not seeds) toasted and crushed fresh — the aroma and tingle fade fast once ground. A little electrifies; much numbs the whole dish.

items.name: Mango ginger
items.prabhava: The turmeric that smells of raw mango — amba haldi bridges two dravyas: haridra's cleansing with amra's fresh scent; the pickle-jar rhizome with a bruise-paste second job.
combinations: shredded fresh with lemon and salt (instant winter pickle)
external paste with lime for sprains and bruises (traditional)
in mixed haldi-amba achar
items.preparation: Fresh rhizome julienned into quick pickles or salads — milder than turmeric, mango-perfumed. Winter-fresh like its cousins, and gentler than both.

items.name: Wild melon powder
items.prabhava: The desert tenderizer — kachri's native enzymes soften meat the way papaya does, while its wild sourness stands in for tomatoes where the desert grows none.
combinations: rubbed into laal maas-style meat marinades
in ker-sangri and desert vegetable dishes
as souring agent where tomato and amchur are absent
items.preparation: Small wild desert melons sliced, sun-dried and powdered. Marinate meat an hour with it; season vegetables with a pinch — sour, funky, unmistakably Rajasthani.

items.name: Alkanet root
items.prabhava: The crimson of rogan josh — ratanjot is a colour dravya: steeped in hot fat it bleeds ruby red, doing with pigment what Kashmiri cooking declines to do with chili heat.
combinations: steeped in hot oil/ghee for rogan josh colour
in traditional hair oils (external)
strained out before serving (colour stays, root goes)
contraindications: internal medicinal use (pyrrolizidine alkaloids — modern hepatotoxicity caution; colour-steeping and straining is the traditional safe use)
items.preparation: Dry root briefly steeped in hot fat and removed — a dye bath, not an ingredient. Traditional use never eats the root itself; keep it that way.

items.name: Wild mustard
items.prabhava: Uttarakhand's crackle — jakhya out-pops mustard in the pahadi tadka: nuttier, wilder, the sound of hill kitchens at dinner time.
combinations: tempered for aloo ke gutke and pahadi potatoes
over hill greens and kandali saag
in place of rai wherever crunch matters
items.preparation: Tiny dark seeds of wild cleome, popped in hot oil like mustard but left crunchy — the crunch is the point. The hill kitchen's signature tempering.

items.name: Wild celery seed
items.prabhava: Ajamoda proper — the classical carminative of the vata formularies: ajmodadi churna's namesake, aimed at wind, colic and stiff joints.
combinations: in ajmodadi churna (classical vata-joint formulation)
with rock salt and warm water for colic (traditional)
pinches in dals where ajwain would go
items.reviewNote: Ajamoda proper (wild celery); batch-25's dravya.celery-seed covers the Bengali radhuni usage — related Apiaceae, kept distinct per predraft identities.
items.preparation: Aromatic wild-celery fruits, chewed in pinches or powdered into formulations. Sits between ajwain and celery in flavour, closer to ajwain in force.

items.name: Coriander-cumin powder
items.prabhava: The gentlest workhorse — dhanyaka cools where jiraka warms, and blended they cancel into a tridosha-friendly base; the reason Gujarati home food digests so quietly.
combinations: the everyday base of Gujarati and Maharashtrian sabzis
with turmeric as the minimal masala trio
in CCF-tea logic (coriander-cumin-fennel) as beverage kin
contraindications: none significant — among the safest of blends
items.preparation: Roasted coriander and cumin ground together, classically 2:1. When in doubt about any stomach, season with dhana-jeera — the blend that offends no dosha.

items.name: Goda masala
items.prabhava: The 'sweet' masala that contains no sugar — dry coconut, sesame and stone flower roasted dark give goda masala its round warmth; Maharashtra's amti tastes of it and nothing else does.
combinations: in amti with kokum or tamarind (the defining dal)
with matki usal and vangi bhaat
roasted coconut-sesame body makes it gentler than garam masala
contraindications: pitta excess in quantity (milder than garam masala)
items.preparation: A dozen-odd spices with dry coconut, sesame and dagad phool, slow-roasted dark and ground. Deeper and rounder than garam masala — warmth without aggression.

items.name: Chaat masala
items.prabhava: The appetite switch — amchur, kala namak and roasted jeera engineered to make the mouth water on contact; chaat masala exists to make you want the next bite.
combinations: over fruit and cucumber (the redeeming use)
on nimbu pani and jaljeera
dusted over chaats — where restraint goes to die
items.preparation: Amchur, black salt, roasted cumin, pepper, hing and dried mint. A pinch turns fruit into appetiser; a heavy hand turns everything into sodium.
